statements.t: Revenue increased 85% over the previous quarter, and AI now accounts for nearly half of our business, all before the expected start of Columbiana colocation billing in January 2027.

The Company’s ten-year take-or-pay colocation agreement with Cerebras, its AI colocation tenant at its Columbiana, Alabama campus is expected to provide annual fees for Phase 1 (15 MW) averaging approximately $40 million per year over the ten-year term, for an approximate aggregate total of $402 million.

The Company expects to provide its tenant with access to the Phase 1 facility on December 15, 2026 and to begin commissioning of the liquid-cooling and power systems at that time, with Phase 1 billing expected to begin in January 2027 following commissioning.
Work on Phase 2 (25 MW) is already underway, and the Company is targeting tenant access for Phase 2 in March 2027.

Based on its contracted business, available power and planned AI infrastructure deployments, the Company expects to reach a revenue run-rate of approximately $250 million to $300 million annualized, or approximately $21 million to $25 million per month, by the end of the third quarter of 2027, subject to adequate financing and market and various other conditions.

The Company expects 2027 capital expenditures of approximately $350 million, primarily for the build-out of approximately 10 MW of AI inference (“token factory”) capacity and the completion of Phase 2 at Columbiana.
The Company intends to fund this program principally through customer deposits and prepayments and debt financing, including the proposed $200 million facility, together with cash on hand.
The Company is targeting the transition of these sites beginning in Q3 and Q4 2027.

We recognize the tax benefit from an uncertain tax position in accordance with ASC 740, Income Taxes, only if it is more likely than not that the tax position will be sustained on examination by the applicable taxing authority, including resolution of the appeals or litigation processes, based on the technical merits of the position.

Our estimates may require periodic adjustments and may not accurately anticipate actual outcomes as resolution of income tax treatments in individual jurisdictions typically would not be known for several years after completion of any fiscal year.
Impairment exists when the carrying value of the company’s asset exceeds the related estimated undiscounted future cash flows expected to be derived from the asset.
